about.title: Lincoln Car Accident Claims
about.longDescription: Lincoln's growth has brought heavier traffic to corridors like Joiner Parkway and Twelve Bridges Drive, and public crash records show injury collisions cluster on Friday afternoons between 4 and 6 p.m., when commuters and weekend errands overlap. In the most recent reporting year, Lincoln saw 48 injury collisions and 61 people hurt on its streets. Behind each of those numbers is someone dealing with medical bills, missed work, and an insurance adjuster who may call before the person has even seen a doctor. LawProactive doesn't handle claims directly — we're a free service that connects injured Lincoln residents with an independent personal injury attorney who can evaluate what happened, help preserve evidence like photos and witness contacts, and speak with insurers so the injured person doesn't have to navigate that alone. Attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless a recovery is made. Reaching out early can make a real difference before evidence disappears or statements are taken out of context.

whyChoose.title: What Matters Legally After a Lincoln Car Accident

items.title: The Clock Starts Running Immediately
items.desc: California generally allows two years to file a car accident claim, but if a government entity (like a city road department) may be involved, that window can shrink to as little as six months. Waiting to seek help can quietly cost someone their right to recover.

items.title: Fault Doesn't Have to Be All-or-Nothing
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning a person can still recover damages even if they were partly responsible for a crash on roads like Ferrari Ranch Road. An attorney can help make sure shared fault doesn't unfairly reduce a fair claim.

items.title: Recorded Statements Can Be Used Against You
items.desc: Insurance adjusters often ask for a recorded statement soon after a crash — before an injured person fully understands their injuries. An independent attorney can advise on what to say, and California places no cap on non-economic damages like pain and suffering, so getting this step right matters.

items.question: How long do I have to file a claim after a car accident in Lincoln?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the crash to file a personal injury lawsuit. If a government entity, such as a city or county road agency, may share responsibility, that deadline can be as short as six months. Because Lincoln's roadways are maintained by different agencies, it's worth having this checked quickly.

items.question: Should I give a recorded statement to the other driver's insurance company?
items.answer: It's generally best to avoid giving a recorded statement before speaking with an attorney. Insurers sometimes use early statements, made before injuries are fully understood, to minimize a claim. An independent attorney connected through LawProactive can advise on communicating with insurers.

items.question: What if the crash happened during Lincoln's busy Friday afternoon traffic?
items.answer: Public records show injury collisions in Lincoln tend to peak on Fridays between 4 and 6 p.m., often along corridors like Lincoln Boulevard and Joiner Parkway. Heavier traffic at that time can mean more witnesses, but also more conflicting accounts, so documenting the scene and contacting an attorney promptly can help preserve important evidence.

items.question: Does it cost anything to talk to an attorney through LawProactive?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and attorneys in our network work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless there's a recovery. There's no obligation to move forward after speaking with someone.
